question.text: A pivotal battle during the Pacific Theatre was this one, taking place in an atoll at the end of the Hawaiian island chain, in which American forces sank four Japanese carriers. An airport in Chicago is named for it.
question.clue: Admiral Nagumo's indecisiveness about bombing the island or carriers left his fleet vulnerable in this battle.

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about famous British explorers who died or disappeared while on their voyages.
swap.text: This explorer gave the name Botany Bay to where he landed in Australia in 1770. This captain of the HMS Endeavour was killed by Hawaiian natives on his third voyage.
swap.clue: The naturalists Daniel Solander and Joseph Banks accompanied this man on that voyage, during which this explorer visited Botany Bay.

question.leadin: This indigenous group massacred the Moriori people on the Chatham Islands. -.
question.text: Name this war-like indigenous group that fought among themselves in the Musket Wars.
question.clue: Tribes of this people experienced bitter infighting in the Musket Wars.

swap.text: Tourists often laugh when they discover that even Hawaii has "interstate highways," something that manylearn upon landing at Daniel Inouye[ee-noh-ay]InternationalAirport in this city.
swap.clue: This capital city of Hawaii. It is home to the only royal palace in the USA, Iolani Palace, as well as Waikiki Beach.

question.text: An agent of the Russian-American company hired by Baranov named Georg Schaffer attempted to overthrow this island country's government in 1815. Its leader was forced to sign the "Bayonet Constitution" in 1887.
question.answerHtml: Kingdom of Hawaii [or the Hawaiian Kingdom or Ke Aupuni Hawaiʻi]
question.clue: Because William C. Lunalilo did not name an heir, supporters of Queen Emma in this nation revolted when David Kalakaua was elected king.

swap.leadin: Jacob Roggeveen was the first recorded European to sight this group of islands.
swap.text: Name this Pacific island group. The US controlled part of this island group has a capital at Pago Pago, and a US National Park exists on its islands of Tutuila, Ta'u, and Ofu.
swap.clue: This country's independence was demanded on "Black Saturday" by the Olaf Frderick Nelson-led Mau Movement.

question.text: The First Fleet of the British Empire arrived at this site of the first penal colony in Australia. It was originally called Stingray Harbour by Cook, but it was changed due to findings by Joseph Banks.
question.clue: Fed by the Georges and Cooks Rivers, its north shore is home to Kingsford Smith airport.

swap.leadin: The successful voyage of this vessel supported the idea that contact between South America and Polynesia happened before the Europeans came.
swap.text: Name the balsa wood raft that crossed the Pacific in 1947.

question.leadin: This country was unified in the 19th century by Tanoa Visawaqa ("ta-NO-ah vees-ah-WA-ka").
question.text: Name this country once home to a chief who was supposedly the most prolific cannibal in history, Udre-Udre ("OO-dre OO-dre"). A racist KKK composed of Australians operated in this Pacific country where an aquifer names a brand of water.
question.clue: After removing Laisenia Qarase (un-guh-RAH-seh) from power, Frank Bainimarama became this country's prime minister.

swap.leadin: The second ruler of this name abolished the tapu code of conduct.
swap.text: Give this name of the ruler who won the Battle of Nuʻuanu to become the first king of a unified Hawaii.
swap.answerHtml: Kamehameha [accept Kamehameha II; accept Kamehameha I or Kamehameha the Great]
swap.clue: The third person of this name was inspired by William Richards to issue the Edict of Toleration and Declaration of Rights, which introduced a legislature and supreme court to his country.

question.text: This New Zealand prime minister, the second woman to hold the office, officially apologized to Samoa in 2002 for injustices during colonial rule. This prime minister also introduced the controversial Foreshore and Seabed Act.

swap.text: Due to a similar story, seven of these figures at Ahu Akivi are thought to depict seven scouts who discovered Rapa Nui. Those examples of these figures are the only ones on Rapa Nui to face the ocean.
swap.answerHtml: moai [prompt on Easter Island heads or Easter Island statues]
swap.clue: A system of ropes likely allowed these objects to "walk" from Rano Raraku to ahu platforms.

question.text: In 1975, Whitlam granted independence to this territory soon after Bougainville seceded as the Republic of the North Solomons. In 1962, Indonesia took over Irian Jaya, the western half of this Melanesian country's main island.
question.answerHtml: Papua New Guinea [or PNG; or Independent State of Papua New Guinea or Independen Stet bilong Papua Niugini or Independen Stet bilong Papua Niu Gini; accept Territory of Papua and New Guinea; prompt on Territory of New Guinea or Territory of Papua]
question.clue: This country is home to a dialect known as Unserdeutsch, or Rabaul Creole, reflecting its former status as Kaiser-Wilhelmsland during German colonization.

swap.text: Scholars have suggested that only the introduction of sweet potato, which supplanted taro and yam, was sufficient to facilitate the labor needed to build many ahu and moai on this island after 1200 CE.
swap.clue: Wooden tablets discovered at this place depict glyphs written in reverse boustrophedon style, the rongorongo script.

question.leadin: Olaf Nelson took over this people's independence movement after its previous leader, Lealofi III of the Tupua Tamasese, was shot and killed by colonial police on Black Saturday, 1929.
question.text: Name this ethnic group whose rival matai chiefs sought backing from the US, UK, and Germany during their 1887 to 1889 "crisis." New Zealand apologized for its role in spreading the 1918 flu pandemic among this people.
question.answerHtml: Sāmoans [or tagata Sāmoa; accept Western Sāmoans; accept American Sāmoans; prompt on Polynesians]
question.clue: That civil war was written about in the book A Footnote to History, by a man who resided at Villa Vailima.

swap.leadin: This leader was elected over his sister Emma and later died in San Francisco on a trip to visit the United States.
swap.text: Name this monarch whose other attempts to bring his kingdom into contact with the rest of the world include a 281-day trip around the world, making him the first monarch to circumnavigate the globe. He signed the Reciprocity Treaty to open up his kingdom to the West.
swap.answerHtml: Kalākaua [or David Laʻamea Kamanakapuʻu Māhinulani Nālaʻiaʻehuokalani Lumialani Kalākaua]

question.text: This favorite wife of Kamehameha, on the other hand, converted to Protestantism and embarked on a campaign of destroying sacred Hawaiian sites and promoting literacy so that Hawaiians could read the Bible.

swap.text: This last King of Hawaii signed the Reciprocity Treaty of 1875 and was forced to sign the Bayonet Constitution. This brother of Liliʻuokalani names the last royal Hawaiian dynasty.

question.leadin: This man's premiership began after he ousted Laisenia Qarase in a 2006 coup.
question.text: Identify this naval commodore who served as Prime Minister of Fiji for 18 years. This man forced President Kaimese Mara to resign in 2000 during a so-called "coup within a coup" while Prime Minister Mahendra Chaudry and his cabinet were being held hostage by George Speight.

swap.leadin: One of these things pertaining to eating prevented different sexes from dining together and was eliminated by a monarch who took power in 1819.
swap.text: Identify these restrictions which helped protect the manna of a person or place. Violating one of these things was sometimes punishable by death.
swap.clue: Another of these laws was imposed to protect the cattle left by George Vancouver's ships.
